description:
Liblice Château was built in 1699–1706 to a design by Giovanni Battista Alliprandi, an Italian architect who designed important buildings for noble families, for Count Arnošt Josef Pachta of Rájov, and it is regarded as a jewel of Baroque architecture.

After the Second World War the state took the property over and placed it under the Czech Academy of Sciences, and it has served as a conference and recreation facility since 1952. It was closed to the public until a large reconstruction, partly funded by EU money, was finished in 2007; it turned the château into a conference and cultural-education centre with a four-star hotel, restaurants and a wellness centre.

Today it still belongs to the Czech Academy of Sciences, with rooms split between the historic château and two modern annexes.

faqs.question: Who designed Liblice Château?
faqs.answer: The Italian architect Giovanni Battista Alliprandi designed it for Count Arnošt Josef Pachta of Rájov, and it was built in 1699–1706.

faqs.question: Who owns the château today?
faqs.answer: After the Second World War the state placed it under the Czech Academy of Sciences, which has run it as a conference and recreation facility since 1952; a 2007 reconstruction added the hotel.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** In Liblice, in the municipality of Byšice near Mělník, about 40 km north of Prague, in Central Bohemia; Booking lists parking with electric charging and accessible parking.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €90/night for a 30 m² Economy Double Room with a double bed, a private bathroom, a flat-screen TV, a minibar and free Wi-Fi, with breakfast included and free cancellation on the rate seen (no prepayment, pay at the property). A 40 m² Deluxe Double Room with a garden view was around €112. Booking shows a small tax charge (about €2) separately.

**On-site:** A restaurant, a spa with a hot tub, gardens, parking and conference facilities.

**Good to know:** The hotel's rooms are split between the historic château and two modern annexes, so ask which building your room is in; entry-level rooms may not be in the château itself. Rates were seen for one February 2027 stay, a low-season date, so check your own dates on Booking.

**Combine with:** [More castle hotels in Czech Republic](/castle-hotels/czech-republic).
